title: Latency-stable batch orchestrator with KV compaction for streaming chat
creator: Liam Chen
description: Problem: Streaming chat completions cause micro-jitter and memory amplification due to long-lived KV cache entries and variable token emission patterns. Current continuous batcher oscillates between tiny microbatches (high scheduling overhead) and large aggregated batches (violates tail latency SLOs). We need an orchestrator that stabilizes latency while reclaiming GPU memory by compacting KV state for idle sessions.
goals: Meet 95th/99th token latency SLO for streaming completions under mixed interactive load
Reduce steady-state GPU KV memory by 20-35% for typical conversational workloads
Introduce heuristics that balance per-session affinity and global throughput without global stall points
non_goals: Full rewrite of the serving runtime (minimal touch approach)
Changing model formats or kernel internals in this ticket
approach: Implement a latency-stable batch orchestrator that enforces a soft microbatch timer plus occupancy floor: each session can hold a microbatch window of X ms but will be forwarded if occupancy or timer triggers
Add per-session KV compaction: periodically serialize small/old KV slots into a compacted representation that keeps only recent top-k attention keys and prunes older low-utility slots
Introduce 'slot pruning' metadata (last_used_ts, token_weight) stored in the host; compaction runs asynchronously to avoid blocking token emission
Allocate GPU memory using alternating slab sizes to reduce fragmentation; prefer packing compacted KV into dense slabs and keep live KV in slab pools optimized for frequent writes
Expose new metrics and tracing hooks (batch_size_distribution, kv_compactions/sec, kv_bytes_reclaimed, slot_prune_count) and tie to autoscaling hints
tradeoffs: Aggressive KV compaction reduces memory but may slightly increase cold-step latency when compacted state must be re-expanded
Per-session heuristics reduce tail jitter for heavy sessions but may underutilize GPU throughput for uniform short requests
Asynchronous compaction adds complexity to correctness (must keep deterministic rehydration ordering)
acceptance_criteria: Under the streaming chat workload benchmark (mixed short/long sessions, 1000 concurrent streams): p95 token latency improves by >=10% vs baseline and p99 does not regress more than 5%
KV memory usage for the benchmark decreases by >=20% without increasing total token cost more than 3%
No correctness regressions in token ordering or chat continuity (automated e2e tests pass)
New metrics emitted and dashboard created in Console; can correlate compactions to memory reclamation
risks: Incorrect rehydration of compacted KV could corrupt past context — must implement strong invariants and exhaustive tests
Timing sensitivity: timers interacting with streaming network jitter could cause oscillation — need hysteresis and smoothing
Scheduler complexity may regress throughput under very high concurrency if not carefully benchmarked
